summary: The English of the six sayings is sound in substance, but the token data was filled mechanically: every sense is '1', and about forty of them name a wrong homograph (Shem, Tob, Rosh, Shual, Adam, 'lamb' for זֶה, 'father' for הַבָּא, 'nose' for אַף, 'where?' for אֵין, 'ploughshare' for אֵת) or the wrong stem; these are re-pointed to the listed Jastrow entries or removed with a note. Every segment literal holds only the last phrase's literal. In 4:18 'ask on his behalf' is corrected to 'question him' against the commentators, and מֻטָּל is the Hofal of נטל (not a Pual of טלל) in both the notes and the morphology. Rambam's causal reading of 4:14 is now recorded rather than 'followed', and several summaries (Bartenura 4:13:7, 4:14:3, 4:16:1; Rambam 4:13:1) are corrected. The model morphology misses the contracted article in seven tokens and the construct state of כֶּתֶר.

value: Two sayings joined in one mishnah: Rabbi Yehuda on care in study, Rabbi Shimon on the three crowns.
שִׁגְגַת תַּלְמוּד עוֹלָה זָדוֹן: a wordplay of opposites, שְׁגָגָה (inadvertent error) and זָדוֹן (deliberate sin). עוֹלָה is 'rises to the level of, counts as'.
עוֹלָה / עוֹלֶה: the same verb used twice, first for an error that 'rises' to deliberate sin, then for the good name that 'rises' above the crowns.
כֶּתֶר is in the construct state throughout: 'crown of Torah', 'crown of priesthood', 'crown of kingship', 'crown of a good name'.
גַּבֵּיהֶן: the plural of גַּב with the suffix -הֶן, referring to the three crowns. כְּתָרִים is masculine (see שְׁלשָׁה); the Mishnah often writes -ן for the 3rd masculine plural ending.
patches.reason: The note says כְּתָרִים is treated as feminine; the numeral שְׁלשָׁה shows it is masculine, and -הֶן is the common Mishnaic spelling of the 3rd plural suffix.

patches.value: Bartenura: the one whose deeds are good and whose reputation is good on their account has no crown in the Torah that obliges honour, yet it rises above all three, because all three need it: a disciple of the sages of ill repute may be disgraced; of a high priest the Gemara (Yoma 71b) says the children of the nations who do Aaron's deeds may come in peace, but not the sons of Aaron who do not; and the king is protected from cursing (Ex 22:27) only when he acts as one of 'your people'.
patches.reason: The summary says a high priest without a good name is 'not obeyed'; Bartenura says he is not greeted in peace, and it leaves out the king.

patches.reason: The stray '-' before 'that' is not English punctuation; the bare 'that' keeps the apposition without it.

גּוֹלֶה is a participle after הֱוֵי: 'be one who goes into exile'.

יְקַיְּמוּהָ: Piel imperfect 3rd masculine plural of קום (Mishnaic קִיֵּם 'make endure, secure'), built with a consonantal yod on the Aramaic pattern, with the 3rd feminine singular suffix -הָ referring to the Torah.
אַל תֹּאמַר and אַל תִּשָּׁעֵן: negative commands use אַל with the jussive-form imperfect.
The Hebrew sets the two clauses by position: the move to a place of Torah is paired with the refusal to rely on colleagues, then on one's own insight.
patches.reason: 'a Piel (here Aramaic-influenced קָם)' is confused: קָם is the Qal; the Piel קִיֵּם has the Aramaic-type strong yod.

patches.value: Bartenura (first reading) and Rabbeinu Yonah take the clause שֶׁחֲבֵרֶיךָ יְקַיְּמוּהָ בְיָדֶךָ as what one must not rely on: colleagues who return from the teacher will not secure the Torah for you. Rambam and Bartenura's second reading take it as the reason for going into exile: only with colleagues does learning endure. The English keeps the bare 'that', which follows the first reading most naturally; the second is recorded. In 4:14.16 the corpus links וְאֶל to BDB אַל 'not'; the token is the preposition אֶל (BDB אֵל), set by a lex override. The words משלי ג at the end are a source marker and are not translated into the saying.
patches.reason: The note claimed the commentators agree; Rambam (normative) and Bartenura's second reading take the clause as causal. The note on וְאֶל is updated for the lex patch.

patches.value: Bartenura: do not rely on your colleagues, when they come from the master's house, to establish the Torah in your hand by teaching you what they learned; go yourself to the master, for hearing from a disciple is unlike hearing from the master. A second reading: I tell you to go into exile because your colleagues will establish it in your hand, for however sharp you are, the Torah endures in you only through the give and take of colleagues; hence 'do not lean on your own understanding'.
patches.reason: The summary named a second explanation without saying what it is; it is a real alternative reading of the clause.

Rambam reads the clause as the reason (with others your learning will endure), against the English, which follows Bartenura's first reading. The commentators differ, so this is 'records', not 'follows'.

patches.value: Rambam (anchored on 4:14.18 but on 4:13): the three good qualities, priesthood, kingship and Torah, were given to Israel at the giving of the Torah; Aaron won priesthood and David kingship, but the crown of Torah lies ready for anyone who wants it, and it is greater than the other two ('by me kings reign', Prov 8:15). The crown of a good name comes from the Torah, from knowing it and doing it.
patches.reason: The summary said only that the comment does not bear on 4:14; it must say what Rambam says.

patches.value: אֵין בְּיָדֵינוּ is kept in its literal, ambiguous form. Bartenura and Rabbeinu Yonah take it as 'we cannot grasp (why the wicked prosper and the righteous suffer)'; Bartenura's second reading, 'in exile we have neither the ease of the wicked nor the sufferings of the righteous', is given in the commentary entry. In 4:15.23 וֶהֱוֵי has the same lemma as הֱוֵי. The BDB entries the corpus gives for אֵין, אַף, אָדָם, רֹאשׁ and שׁוּעָל are wrong homographs (where?, nose, Adam, Rosh, Shual); lex overrides point to the Jastrow entries.
patches.reason: Updates the note for the lex patches.

value: The saying is a simile (דּוֹמֶה לְ) followed by an imperative drawing the practical consequence.
בִּפְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא: 'before the world to come', in front of it as an entrance hall is in front of the hall.
הַתְקֵן is a Hiphil imperative of תקן: 'make ready, put in order'; the object is the reflexive עַצְמְךָ.
פְּרוֹזְדוֹר and טְרַקְלִין are Greek loanwords; טְרַקְלִין is triklinion, a dining hall. The first is the entrance room, the second the inner hall.
הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא is the standard term for the world to come; הַבָּא is a participle used as an adjective.
patches.reason: 'prozdor' is the Hebrew word in Latin letters, not a Greek form.

patches.value: Bartenura: פְּרוֹזְדוֹר is a gatehouse; the Targum renders the biblical אוּלָם (porch) by פְּרוֹזְדוֹרָא.
patches.reason: The summary reverses the Targum: Targum translates אוּלָם as פְּרוֹזְדוֹרָא, not the other way.

patches.value: פְּרוֹזְדוֹר has no lexicon key in the pack; it is 'vestibule', Bartenura's 'gatehouse' (the Targum's word for אוּלָם, porch). טְרַקְלִין is 'the great hall', Bartenura 'the king's seat', Rambam 'the palace hall'; the pack's Jastrow entry is a cross-reference only. כְּדֵי is the preposition כְּ with דַּי 'enough', 'so that' before שֶׁ.
patches.reason: Corrects the Targum reference and Rambam's word (הֵיכָל, palace hall).

patches.value: The corpus links קוֹרָה to BDB 'rafter, beam', which does not fit; a lex override points to Jastrow's קוֹרָה II 'cold, cooling' (קוֹרַת רוּחַ, satisfaction). 'Spiritual contentment' renders the idiom; the literal sense is in the phrase note. The subject of הוּא is Rabbi Yaakov of 4:16 per the plain sequence.
patches.reason: Updates the note for the lex patch.

patches.value: Rabbi Shimon son of Elazar says: Do not appease your fellow at the time of his anger, and do not comfort him at the time when his dead lies before him, and do not question him at the time of his vow, and do not strive to see him at the time of his disgrace.
patches.reason: תִּשְׁאַל לוֹ is to question him: Rabbeinu Yonah 'שלא ישאל ממנו הפתחים' (do not ask of him the openings), and Bartenura's openings are put to the vower ('he will say, I vowed with that in mind'). 'Ask on his behalf' implies petitioning a third party.

value: Four prohibitions, each with the same shape: אַל + verb + the person + בִשְׁעַת (at the time of) + his state.
אַל תְּרַצֶּה אֶת חֲבֵרְךָ: the Piel of רצה governs the direct object marked by אֶת.
תְּנַחֲמֶנּוּ: Piel imperfect 2nd masculine singular with the 3rd masculine singular suffix joined by an energic nun (-ֶנּוּ), as often on the imperfect.
מֵתוֹ מֻטָּל לְפָנָיו: מֻטָּל is the Hofal participle of נטל ('cast, lay'), the nun assimilated into the doubled ט: his dead 'lies before him', the time between death and burial.
תִּשְׁאַל לוֹ בִשְׁעַת נִדְרוֹ: 'question him'; the commentators explain it as probing for openings (פְּתָחִים) to release the vow while he is still angry.
The repeated בִשְׁעַת / בְּשָׁעָה gives the saying its rhythm: the right time matters as much as the act.
patches.reason: The energic nun is not a feature 'after אַל'; מֻטָּל needs its root; the note on תִּשְׁאַל לוֹ follows the corrected English.

patches.value: שָׁעָה is 'hour, moment', rendered 'at the time of'. תִּשְׁאַל לוֹ is to question the vower: Bartenura (seek openings to release his vow, for he will answer each that he vowed with it in mind) and Rabbeinu Yonah (do not ask of him the openings) agree. מֻטָּל is the Hofal participle of נטל; the corpus links it to טָלַל, the wrong root. תִּשְׁתַּדֵּל is the Hitpael of שׁדל, 'make an effort, strive'.
patches.reason: The note claimed both commentators read 'on his behalf'; Rabbeinu Yonah says 'ממנו', of him. It also records the root of מֻטָּל.
The parse leaves out the gender: שְׁלשָׁה is the form used with masculine nouns (כְּתָרִים).
כֶּתֶר תּוֹרָה is a construct chain; the segolate construct has the same form as the absolute.
כֶּתֶר is bound to the next noun (construct, not absolute); and the form had a dagesh in כ that the token, after וְ, does not have.

The suffix refers to the masculine כְּתָרִים (cf. שְׁלשָׁה); -הֶן is the usual Mishnaic spelling of the 3rd plural suffix and is not feminine here. Proposed: masculine.
The patah and the dagesh in ת show the article contracted into the preposition (בַּ = בְּ + הַ); the analysis leaves it out.
The qamets before א shows the contracted article (לָ = לְ + הָ, 'to the lions'); the analysis leaves it out.
רֹאשׁ is not bound to a following noun: לַשּׁוּעָלִים follows with לְ. It is absolute, as is the parallel זָנָב לָאֲרָיוֹת.
The patah and the dagesh in ש show the contracted article (לַ = לְ + הַ); the analysis leaves it out.
בַ with patah is בְּ + הַ: 'in the vestibule'; the analysis leaves out the article.
The form of the second morpheme had a dagesh in ד that the token does not have; forms are copied as printed.
לַ with the dagesh in ט is לְ + הַ: 'to the hall'; the lemma had the dagesh of the article, which the absolute singular does not have.
The qamets of בָּ before ע is the contracted article (בָּעוֹלָם 'in the world'); the analysis leaves it out.

קוֹרַת רוּחַ is 'coolness of spirit' (Jastrow קוֹרָה II 'cold, cooling'), from the root קרר 'to be cold'; קור is not the root of this sense. Proposed: קרר.

patches.reason: מֻטָּל is the Hofal participle of נטל (Hifil הֵטִיל 'cast, lay down'), the nun assimilated into the doubled ט. A Pual of טלל would be מְטֻלָּל.
The form of the noun had a dagesh in פ that the token, after לְ, does not have; forms are copied as printed.
The lemma is the singular absolute נֶדֶר (two segols); נֵדֶר is not a form of the word.

verdicts.comment: The English follows the first reading; the second (causal) reading is now in the summary and the phrase note.
The comment is on 4:13 (anchored on 4:14.18); its point, that the good name comes from Torah, agrees with 4:13's 'rises above them'.

Rambam reads שֶׁחֲבֵרֶיךָ as causal (with others your learning endures). The English stands because Bartenura's first reading (normative) and Rabbeinu Yonah take the clause as what one must not rely on; the normative commentators differ, and the relation is patched to 'records'.
Anchored on 4:17.11 but on 4:18: the four prohibitions are moral rules on the right time; the English agrees.
Bartenura's openings are put to the vower, who answers each; the English 'ask on his behalf' implied a third party. Fixed by the patch to 'question him'.
